target_customer: African migrants and diaspora in Europe, plus freelancers, e-merchants and small importers who move money between Europe, the US and Africa
problem: Migrants face costly remittances and poor access to European bank accounts. Moneco offers a euro account, a card and low cost transfers aimed at them.
business_model: Consumer fintech app: card interchange, FX and remittance fees
product_category: Neobank and remittance app for diaspora

founders.name: Shams Radjabaly
education: Educated in France (institution not named on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: born in Madagascar, lived in Singapore and the US, worked in Morocco, background in financial markets and management consulting.

founders.name: Bilal Dahlab
founders.background_notes: YC page: raised in Geneva, experience in strategic consulting, finance, energy and blockchain. Employers and education not named.

founders.name: Kuassi Jimmy Kumako
founders.background_notes: Born in Benin per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs banking partner integrations, card issuing and compliance for several corridors, standard fintech engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Licences and partners are shared infrastructure; community trust is the only differentiator and remittance rivals target the same users.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from sources dated at founding; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: The YC page frames migrants as underserved with expensive banking and remittances. No dated spend figures were found.

identity.logo: Simple wordmark with green accent (colors inferred from logo files)
identity.visual_style: Lifestyle photos, phone mockups, green accent
identity.voice_and_tone: Informal French with tu, benefit led headlines

branding.brand_signature: Positioning as the financial app of Africans

brand_strength.rationale: Clear audience focus but little press on the brand itself; app ratings 4.0 to 4.5 on stores per its site.

pivots.from: Euro neobank for migrants in Europe
pivots.to: Euro, US and USDC accounts for Africans broadly, with Canadian entity
pivots.why: Not stated; observed from website and Wefunder listing

outcome_analysis: Moneco is still active with a team of about 15. Funding evidence is thin and conflicting, including a small Wefunder crowdfunding raise in 2025, which suggests slow capital progress. No shutdown or exit was found, so the outcome is unresolved and the license and distribution questions remain open.
notes: Unverified funding: Wefunder snippet says $124,000 from 275 investors, last funded March 2025 (page returned 403); a May 2026 Liners report cites about $146,700; Village.ai and Signalbase say $3.3M total; CB Insights says $620K over 5 rounds; Wefunder text also says $1.5M from YC, Kima Ventures, Soma Ventures. Kima Ventures as investor appears in aggregators only. Competitor search found only 2025 era sources (LemFi, Afriex), so the list is empty. Outcome search found no news about Moneco. Completeness pass: two rounds recorded, each from a single outlet: a seed dated January 2023 with no amount (Liners) and a Wefunder crowdfunding raise of about 124K USD in March 2025 (Wefunder, matching CB Insights convertible note of 0.12M on 2025-03-05). Reported totals conflict (620K CB Insights, 1M Liners and Village, 3.3M Signalbase) and are not summed, so the recorded rounds are a partial history.
